tasks.short: Research, select and implement benefits that address employees' needs within an agreed budget.

steps.what: Collect benefits uptake, costs and recurring employee requests.
Discuss unmet needs and access barriers with employee representatives.
Compare broker proposals, coverage terms and exclusions.

loop.input: Provider proposals and current benefits policies.
loop.output: A comparison table with coverage, exclusions, prices, dates and source passages.
loop.check: Validate required fields and price arithmetic; a specialist checks material exclusions against cited passages.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per document; missing or conflicting terms go to a specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Proposal layouts and coverage wording vary; fixed parsers cannot reliably identify equivalent terms.

steps.what: Calculate package costs under different eligibility and uptake assumptions.
Discuss service terms, affordability and coverage gaps with the broker.
Approve the benefits package, spending and implementation conditions.
Set eligibility, contribution amounts and enrolment dates.
Prepare and send the benefits announcement and enrolment instructions.

tasks.design: A reusable benefits register and comparison template in {WORKFLOW} combine aggregate {HCM} data with source-linked proposal extraction from {DOCS}. Deterministic calculations produce cost scenarios; approved choices configure {HCM} and populate announcement templates in {EMAIL}. People retain consultation, negotiation and package approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Coverage terms arrive in inconsistent documents, while costs and employee needs sit in separate records. Bespoke comparisons and integrations were costly relative to an occasional package review.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building comparison forms, calculations and connectors. Bounded extraction can populate a fixed comparison schema, with specialist review of consequential terms.
tasks.still_hard: Employee value depends on access, exclusions and personal circumstances, not just uptake. GDPR limits the use of sensitive information; national rules determine consultation and benefit-change obligations.
tasks.human_edge: Understand whose needs are missing from aggregate demand and negotiate meaningful access without promising coverage the provider has not agreed.

ambition.what: Quarterly benefits access reviews for shift workers who cannot attend daytime sessions.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time assembling comparisons and more time testing access barriers with employees. A delegated pilot budget could allow small access trials; that delegation requires explicit agreement.

reach.task: Identify benefits access problems during onboarding.
reach.learn: Interview employees without collecting unnecessary health details and distinguish awareness problems from coverage gaps.
Read exclusions, validate contribution calculations and explain uncertainty in coverage comparisons.

evidence.claim: Fixed comparison schemas, cost calculations and approved notification templates can use deterministic software.
A study covering workers in Denmark, including HR occupations, found modest chatbot time savings; it does not establish savings for this benefits workflow.

assumptions: The reusable starter contains comparison fields, scenario formulas and synthetic examples; employer data requires authorized access.
Low uptake is treated as a signal for investigation, not proof that a benefit lacks value.
The priors understate the structured cost work, but correctly emphasize judgement and employee relationships.
Build ranges estimate working effort for one jurisdiction and a small provider set; consultation and provider response time can extend elapsed delivery.
unknowns: Current providers, benefit types and renewal dates.
Availability and quality of enrolment, cost and employee-request records.
Applicable countries, collective agreements and employee-representation arrangements.
Who may approve spending, provider commitments and pilot budgets.
research_questions: How reliably can proposal extraction identify exclusions and waiting periods across representative documents?
Which participation measures reveal access barriers without exposing sensitive employee circumstances?
new_work: Review extracted coverage terms and resolve ambiguous exclusions.
Maintain provider comparison fields, contribution rules and announcement templates.
Investigate missing data and small-group privacy risks.
Check whether launched benefits reach the groups identified during consultation.

tasks.short: Develop benefits selection tools and compensation guidance that make policy understandable and decisions traceable.

steps.what: Gather employee and manager problems with existing benefits and compensation guidance.
Translate policy into eligibility rules, decision guidance and acceptance examples.

loop.input: Approved policies, pay bands and tool requirements.
loop.output: Draft decision tables, policy references, unresolved questions and acceptance examples.
loop.check: Require a source for each rule; specialists resolve conflicts and approve executable interpretations.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass per policy version; unresolved rules remain disabled.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative policies contain exceptions and qualifications that require interpretation before deterministic implementation.

steps.what: Configure the employee benefits selector and its eligibility rules.
Build a compensation calculator using pay bands, budgets and policy limits.
Test representative employee and manager journeys, including exceptions and accessibility.
Approve the tools for release after reviewing results and unresolved risks.
Release the approved benefits selector to eligible employees.
Publish the approved compensation calculator and manager instructions.

tasks.design: Start with a reusable rule catalogue and acceptance examples in {DOCS}, then configure benefits selection in {HCM}. Where existing compensation guidance is insufficient, build a deterministic calculator in {WORKFLOW}, using approved pay bands and budget limits, with access through {DOCS}. A bounded loop drafts policy tables; meaningful human approval remains on release and individual compensation decisions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Policy interpretation, interface development and acceptance testing needed different specialists. Small guidance tools often remained in {SPREADSHEET} because a maintained application was too expensive.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding can accelerate forms, calculation engines and test fixtures. Existing {HCM} configuration may already cover benefits selection, avoiding a separate application.
tasks.still_hard: Policy rules can be internally inconsistent, and understandable guidance needs testing with real users. GDPR applies to personal data and significant automated decisions; model use that influences employment decisions needs EU AI Act assessment, with consultation under applicable national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Choose which decisions the tool should support, recognize misleading precision and test whether employees understand the consequences of their choices.

ambition.what: An employee benefits comparison service showing personal contributions and coverage differences before enrolment.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends more time testing guidance with users and examining policy exceptions. Decision rights do not change automatically; the tools expose permitted options and route compensation approvals to authorized people.

reach.learn: Explain displayed costs, recognize accessibility barriers and escalate coverage questions.
Write decision tables and independent acceptance examples, including rounding, effective dates and boundary cases.

evidence.claim: Benefits eligibility and compensation scenario calculations can use approved deterministic rules without model-generated pay recommendations.
AFAS Profit 8 records job schemes for pay transparency; this supports a structured reward-data foundation, not a complete benefits selection service.

assumptions: The benefits selector uses existing {HCM} functionality where available.
A separate calculator is justified only where configuration cannot express approved scenarios.
The tools display policy-based choices and calculations; they do not autonomously award pay or determine disputed coverage.
The conversation-heavy prior describes requirements and testing; the proposed tool itself is mainly deterministic.
Build estimates cover one policy family and authorized test data, including consultation effort where applicable; elapsed approval time may be longer.
unknowns: Approved pay bands, benefit rules and tax assumptions.
Compensation approval authority and existing consultation agreements.
Whether personal calculations can run without retaining sensitive selections.
research_questions: Can users distinguish an illustrative calculation from a binding entitlement?
Which policy boundary cases require specialist interpretation rather than executable rules?
Can the configured selector meet accessibility needs without a separate interface?
new_work: Maintain policy versions, effective dates and independent calculation examples.
Review rule changes before release and retire outdated tool versions.
Test accessibility and comprehension with employees and managers.
Monitor exceptions, incorrect assumptions and access permissions.

tasks.short: Administer and review benefits programs, including controlled integration after mergers and acquisitions.

steps.what: Inventory employee enrolments, plan dates and contribution arrangements.
Compare plan terms, protected entitlements and renewal obligations.

loop.input: Plan documents, provider contracts and relevant employee terms.
loop.output: An obligations register with coverage, contribution, renewal and grandfathering clauses linked to sources.
loop.check: Validate dates and amounts; a specialist verifies material clauses and obtains legal interpretation where needed.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per document; conflicting or unclear obligations remain unresolved.
loop.why_not_simpler: Legacy documents express obligations in varied prose that cannot safely be mapped by field names alone.

steps.what: Map legacy employee identifiers, benefit codes and contribution fields.
Model renewal or harmonization options, costs and employee impacts.
Consult employee representatives and affected groups on proposed changes.
Approve the transition plan, protected exceptions and implementation dates.
Update plan settings and migrate approved employee enrolments.
Submit enrolment changes to benefits providers.
Check payroll deductions against approved enrolments and provider confirmations.

tasks.design: A versioned benefits register in {WORKFLOW} links plan obligations in {DOCS} to employee mappings from {HCM}. Deterministic scenario calculations and migration checks prepare approved changes for {HCM} and {PARTNER_PORTAL}, then reconcile confirmations against {PAYROLL}. A bounded loop extracts clauses; people decide interpretation, consultation outcomes and transition terms.
tasks.previous_blocker: Legacy identifiers, plan codes and contractual exceptions differ across businesses. One-off mapping work and provider-specific submissions made reusable integration expensive.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding can reduce the cost of mapping utilities, validation reports and provider adapters. Document extraction helps build an obligations register without replacing legal or employee-relations judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Accrued rights, pension arrangements and transaction-specific promises may prevent simple harmonization. GDPR, applicable EU AI Act requirements and national transfer, consultation and employment rules need assessment; acquisition data access may be restricted.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize when an apparently equal package removes a valued entitlement, and negotiate a credible transition with affected employees.

ambition.what: A monthly benefits continuity review of unresolved enrolment and deduction mismatches.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time reconciling files and more time resolving contractual differences and transition risks. They can prioritize remediation within the approved plan; authority to change entitlements remains explicitly assigned.

reach.task: Reconcile benefit deductions after enrolment changes.
reach.learn: Trace effective dates, retroactive adjustments and provider confirmations without silently overwriting discrepancies.
Interpret cohort-level impact reports and separate negotiable changes from protected obligations.

evidence.claim: Identifier mapping, effective-date validation, migration controls and payroll reconciliation are primarily deterministic integration work.
Extraction can prepare an obligations register, but contractual interpretation and benefit harmonization still require specialist judgement.

assumptions: Routine reviews use the inventory, scenario and reconciliation steps; legacy mapping and migration apply when plans or businesses are combined.
No employee is assigned a reduced entitlement solely from an automated mapping.
Authorized files can replace unavailable interfaces; the high API prior is not assumed to hold for every provider.
Build ranges cover a limited plan set and two legacy data structures, not an entire multinational acquisition.
Consent and access ranges include consultation effort where applicable; statutory processes and transaction restrictions may extend elapsed delivery.
unknowns: Acquisition scope, jurisdictions and transaction stage.
Protected or grandfathered benefits and applicable agreements.
Legacy identifiers, data quality and lawful data-sharing arrangements.
Provider submission formats, acknowledgements and correction windows.
Payroll cutoffs and authority for migration and external submissions.
research_questions: Which migration controls detect coverage loss before any provider submission?
How should conflicting effective dates be represented without silently selecting one?
Which plan obligations require jurisdiction-specific legal interpretation?
new_work: Maintain mappings, obligation versions and provider adapters.
Review ambiguous clauses and unmatched employee records.
Approve migration controls and enrolment submission batches.
Investigate deduction exceptions and monitor coverage continuity after transition.

tasks.short: Help employees resolve benefits questions and disputes with providers while preserving trust and appropriate escalation.

steps.what: Read incoming benefits questions and record the issue and urgency.

loop.input: An employee enquiry and a fixed routing taxonomy.
loop.output: A case category, requested action and routing flags, retaining only necessary details.
loop.check: Validate the schema and employee identity separately; explicit urgent terms override classification.
loop.stop: One classification pass per enquiry; ambiguity, sensitive narratives or uncertain urgency go to a person.
loop.why_not_simpler: Employees describe the same benefits issue in varied language that fixed forms do not capture.

steps.what: Check recorded enrolment, eligibility dates and contribution details.
Find relevant policy terms and prepare the case background.

loop.input: The enquiry, verified enrolment facts and authorized current policy passages.
loop.output: A case brief with cited clauses, factual discrepancies and questions for the employee or provider.
loop.check: Check policy version, access rights and citations; a specialist verifies any interpretation before use.
loop.stop: Retrieve at most five passages and allow one revision; conflicting or missing evidence triggers specialist handling.
loop.why_not_simpler: Matching a narrative question to relevant policy clauses needs language interpretation beyond keyword retrieval.

steps.what: Listen to the employee and clarify the problem and desired outcome.
Ask the provider to explain or investigate the disputed issue.
Decide an escalation or permitted employer remedy within delegated authority.
Explain the outcome, remaining uncertainty and next steps to the employee.

loop.input: The approved resolution, provider response and verified case facts.
loop.output: A plain-language reply stating the outcome, limitations and next steps.
loop.check: Match every substantive statement to approved facts; a specialist checks tone, privacy and absence of new promises.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; sensitive or disputed explanations are written by the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Contested cases need contextual explanations that fixed templates often fail to express clearly.

steps.what: Record the outcome, follow-up date and any reusable service issue.

tasks.design: Configure case tracking and follow-up in {HELPDESK}, with authorized enrolment lookup from {HCM} and a versioned policy collection in {DOCS}. Bounded loops classify enquiries, prepare cited briefs and draft approved explanations; {EMAIL} sends replies after review. Human conversations handle distress, disputed coverage and provider mediation, while structured case outcomes reveal recurring service problems.
tasks.previous_blocker: Case facts, enrolment records and policy wording were spread across a mailbox and several systems. A generic answer service could retrieve information but could not safely resolve contested facts or preserve the relationship.
tasks.enabler_now: Small integrations can supply verified facts to a constrained drafting process. Existing {HELPDESK} routing, permissions and reminders can handle the routine coordination.
tasks.still_hard: Medical and family circumstances can make cases highly sensitive. GDPR requires an appropriate lawful basis, special-category conditions where relevant, limited sharing and retention; national rules affect employer responsibilities, and EU AI Act applicability depends on the actual use.
tasks.human_edge: Hear what the employee is worried about, challenge an inadequate provider response and explain limits without dismissing the person.

ambition.what: A tracked benefits dispute service with a named case owner and agreed follow-up date.

tasks.altitude: The manager handles fewer searches and status chases and spends more time on difficult conversations and recurring provider failures. Decision rights remain within existing employer delegations and provider coverage authority.

reach.task: Triage benefits enquiries and maintain follow-up dates.
reach.learn: Recognize urgency, minimize sensitive case notes and hand over contested matters with verified facts.

reach.task: Support an employee whose benefits dispute becomes a grievance.
reach.learn: Use the case chronology, preserve employee voice and distinguish provider decisions from employer commitments.

evidence.claim: Case routing, verified record lookup and follow-up reminders can be configured or implemented deterministically; mediation remains interpersonal.
IBM's AskHR case reports an early fall in HR NPS when managers lost HR partners and the phone line; this supports retaining accessible human help.

assumptions: The steps describe a mediated case; straightforward factual questions can skip the conversation, provider investigation and remedy decision.
Employer case records exclude detailed medical claims unless handling them is necessary and lawful.
Automatic case completion requires a recorded outcome and no outstanding action; sending a reply alone does not close a dispute.
The human-heavy prior fits mediation, while preparation and record keeping remain open to automation.
Build ranges cover one shared case queue and policy collection, including applicable consultation effort; elapsed access approval can take longer.
unknowns: Case volumes and the mix of factual questions, sensitive cases and disputes.
Current provider escalation routes and response commitments.
Who may access enrolment facts and sensitive case material.
Lawful sharing arrangements, retention periods and employee-representation requirements.
Delegated remedy limits and available human support channels.
research_questions: Does routing reliably surface urgent situations without retaining unnecessary sensitive detail?
Can reviewers verify draft explanations faster than writing them while maintaining accuracy and empathy?
Which recurring issues should become policy improvements rather than reusable replies?
new_work: Review cited briefs and outgoing explanations.
Handle classification uncertainty, missing facts and stale policy passages.
Maintain escalation contacts, permissions and retention settings.
Audit unresolved follow-ups and convert recurring provider problems into service improvements.

role.altitude: The role shifts from assembling comparisons and chasing records toward evaluating access, testing policy choices and resolving difficult cases. Broader authority would require explicit delegation; faster preparation does not itself grant the right to change pay or benefits.
reach: Help compensation and benefits specialists turn policy into tested decision tables.
Help payroll clerks trace benefit deductions across enrolments, effective dates and provider confirmations.
Help human resources assistants run a reliable benefits case service.
Work with labor relations specialists on evidence-based consultation and protected entitlements.
skills_to_grow: Policy modelling with effective dates, exceptions and independent calculation checks.
Benefits cost analysis and careful interpretation of participation data.
Accessible user testing and plain-language explanation of uncertainty.
Privacy-aware case handling and meaningful review of model drafts.
Provider negotiation, employee consultation and migration control.
role.ambitious_version: Run a benefits access and continuity service that combines quarterly reviews for underserved employees, understandable selection tools and tracked dispute resolution. Use the evidence to propose targeted improvements within an agreed budget and approval framework.
